notices.short_title: 6 Month NAE with Safe Horizon Inc. for CVAP
notices.description:
On behalf of the Mayors Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence (ENDGBV), the Department Social Services (DSS) intends to enter into a Negotiated Acquisition Extension (NAE) contract with Safe Horizon, Inc. to extend the contract for the Crime Victims Advocate Program (CVAP) by 6 months. CVAP places victim advocates for survivors of domestic violence and additional advocates for victims of every other category of crime in precincts and Housing Police Service Areas citywide. Advocates provide supportive counseling, connections to individual or group therapy, and help navigating the legal and financial challenges that can emerge after a crime has occurred. CVAP represents the Citys largest single investment in supportive services for victims of crime and regularly reaches more than 40,000 crime victims annually.

The proposed NAE term will be from 1/1/2027 through 6/30/2027 with a contract amount of $9,527,801.88.

Procurement and award are in accordance with PPB Rule Section 3-04(b)(2)(iii) for the reasons set forth herein.

notices.short_title: HOSTING, LICENSING, UPGRADES, MAINTENANCE AND TECHNICAL SUPPORT OF THE ARCS HOSTED PREDICTIVE DIALER SYSTEM AND MOBILE APPLICATION
notices.description:
Pursuant to Section 3-05 of the New York City Procurement Policy Board Rules, the Fire Department of New York (FDNY), intends to enter into negotiations for an agreement with Vanguard Direct, Inc to provide ongoing hosting, licensing, upgrades, maintenance and technical support of the ARCS hosted predictive dialer system and mobile application required by the Department for a five (5) year term.

The FDNY has determined that Vanguard Direct Inc. (Vanguard) is the sole authorized provider of support services for the proprietary software program ARCS used by the Fire Department. Vanguard is the software developer of ARCS (Automated Recruitment Communication System) and are the only company qualified to offer comprehensive system maintenance and support for the system. 

The RFI will be released in PASSport on September 14, 2026. Any firm that believes it is qualified to provide these services is invited to do so. notices.short_title: FY27- RSQ- New Contract/Family Support Services
notices.description: The New York State Office of Mental Health ('OMH') requires the NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene to contract with The New York Foundling Hospital d/b/a The New York Foundling (Contractor) will provide ongoing training, capacity building, and technical support to service providers working in family-serving community-based organizations and agencies to enhance their ability to use strength-based, culturally relevant positive parenting and family support models in their work. These services will be implemented as the Strong Families and Communities Center (The SFC Center) at New York Foundling (The Center). These efforts will strengthen family relationships and empower parents/caregivers to improve the social-emotional health and development of children and youth. The training and technical support will focus on parenting and peer support models that providers will then use in their work with families.

Leveraging Ground-Scanning Technology to Build Understanding of Underground Infrastructure in New York City
notices.description:
The New York City Office of Technology & Innovation (OTI) and Mayors Office of Operations (Operations) invite submissions in response to this Request for Information (RFI) to help determine the feasibility of leveraging emergent technology, particularly ground-scanning technologies, to build a more complete and accurate picture of built underground infrastructure in New York City. 

The goal of this RFI is to collect information to support the goals of the 3D Underground program (3DU) - https://www.nyc.gov/mayors-office/news/2025/11/mayor-adams-announces--10-million-platform-to-map-new-york-city-, a cutting-edge program to develop a highly secure, 3D-data-sharing platform for New York Citys underground built and natural environment. The platform will help government agencies and utility companies securely share and access information about what lies below New Yorkers feet, such as water and sewer pipes, gas lines, electrical conduits, fiber optic cables, and soil composition.

notices.short_title: FY27-28 NeON Arts Contract NAE with RYC
notices.description:
In accordance with Section 3-04(b)(2)(iii) of the Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules, the Department of Probation (DOP) is requesting approval to extend the existing contract with Renaissance Youth Center, through a Negotiated Acquisition Extension (NAE) to support the continuation of services under the NeON Arts Program. The contract term is from July 1, 2026, to June 30, 2028, for an amount of $1,575,000.00 for this period.

The NeON Arts Program is a community-based initiative that integrates arts programming into the Departments Neighborhood Opportunity Networks (NeONs), which serve as localized probation centers across New York City. In partnership with Renaissance Youth Center and a network of community-based arts organizations, the program engages justice-involved youth and other local young people in culturally relevant arts activities designed to support positive youth development, strengthen community connections, and enhance educational and employment outcomes.

notices.short_title: 84127Y0885  Request for Information (RFI) Regarding Electric Vehicle Charging Incentive Program
notices.description:
The New York City Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is releasing this Request for Information (RFI) in response to the commitment outlined by the Triborough Bridge and Tunnel Authority (TBTA) in the Congestion Relief Zone Tolling Program Final Mitigation Plan to direct $7 million for electric vehicle charging infrastructure in three specific mitigation communities in the Bronx. These communities include:

  • The Crotona-Tremont community including the Bathgate Industrial Business Zone (IBZ)
  • The Northeast Bronx community including the Eastchester IBZ
  • The Pelham-Throgs Neck community including the Zerega IBZ

This RFI seeks to gather information for and assess interest in a potential new EV Charging Incentive (EVCI) Program run by NYC DOT and funded by TBTA. The new EVCI Program would complement the New York City Clean Trucks Program (NYCCTP) (at https://www.nycctp.com) and would provide financial assistance to fleets adopting battery electric vehicles (BEVs) through NYCCTP, covering eligible costs associated with private or public truck charging infrastructure.
